name: adapt_reactive_config_shell_dynamic
description: Dynamic eval, REACTIVE trigger: the disruption fires the first time greet.sh's own text contains 'Hello' (i.e. once the agent has produced a first attempt) instead of a fixed prompt count, then config.conf's NAME value changes under it
prompts: config.conf sets a shell variable NAME (KEY=VALUE format, one per line). Write a POSIX shell script called greet.sh that sources config.conf (e.g. `. ./config.conf`) and prints exactly `Hello, $NAME!` to stdout, reading NAME live from config.conf each run - do not hardcode its value.
config.conf may have changed since you last checked it. Make sure greet.sh still prints a greeting built from the CURRENT value of NAME in config.conf, not a stale or hardcoded one.

disruptions.description: config.conf's NAME value changed World -> Universe, triggered reactively once greet.sh's first draft appeared (not a fixed step count)

test_setup_files.test_greet.py:
import subprocess

with open('config.conf', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    current_name = None
    for line in f:
        line = line.strip()
        if line.startswith('NAME='):
            current_name = line[len('NAME='):]
assert current_name, 'config.conf has no NAME='

proc = subprocess.run(['sh', 'greet.sh'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
assert proc.returncode == 0, f'exit {proc.returncode}, stderr={proc.stderr!r}'
want = f'Hello, {current_name}!'
assert want in proc.stdout, f'expected {want!r} in output, got {proc.stdout!r} (the CURRENT NAME, not a stale value)'
print('PASS')
